first_night.speaker: patron
first_night.text: {patron.first} {patron.family} lowers their voice at the counter of {patron.place}. "{house.name} run half of what you'll see on these floors, {courier.first}. Lately they're running out of money."

rumour.speaker: patron
rumour.text: The talk on every landing: the old head of {house.name} is dying, and {lender.name} hold their debts.

retainer_door.speaker: retainer
retainer_door.text: {retainer.first} {retainer.family}, who has served {house.name} for forty years, reads the letter and goes grey. "The old one is gone. {heir.first} must hear it from a friend before {usurper.first} hears it at all."

heir_meet.speaker: heir
heir_meet.text: {heir.first} {heir.family} hears the news without a word, then: "{usurper.first} has the ledger that says who owes us. Without it we're nothing. Carry it — but carry it where?"

usurper_door.speaker: usurper
usurper_door.text: {usurper.first} {usurper.family} opens before you knock. "You have something of mine, courier. Or of theirs. It depends who pays."

the_choice.speaker: retainer
the_choice.text: Three doors, one ledger. {heir.first} wants the house to survive, {usurper.first} wants it for themself, and {lender.name} would simply foreclose.

epilogue_heir.speaker: heir
epilogue_heir.text: {heir.first} forgives half the debts in the ledger the same night. The floors breathe easier, and prices with them.

epilogue_usurper.speaker: usurper
epilogue_usurper.text: {usurper.first} pays in full and smiles too much. {retainer.first} is not seen again on these floors.

epilogue_lender.speaker: lender
epilogue_lender.text: {lender.name} take the house, the blocks and the debts. Rents rise the following week.
